facts.statement: Unwindia was a pterodactyloid pterosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now Brazil.
facts.quote: Unwindia is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (Albian stage) of what is now modern-day Brazil.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was obtained by the German State Museum of Natural History Karlsruhe from an illegal digger near Santana do Cariri in the Araripe Basin.
facts.quote: The German State Museum of Natural History Karlsruhe obtained a pterosaur fossil from an illegal commercial digger who had found it somewhere near Santana do Cariri in the Araripe Basin.

facts.statement: David Martill named and described the species Unwindia trigonus in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, the specimen was named and described as the type species Unwindia trigonus by David Martill.

facts.statement: The genus name Unwindia honors the British pterosaur expert David Unwin.
facts.quote: The generic name honours the British pterosaur expert David Unwin.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the snout fragment is 221 mm.
facts.quote: The preserved length of the snout fragment of Unwindia is 221 mm.

facts.statement: Unwindia has a unique specialization of seven pairs of teeth located entirely in front of the nasoantorbital fenestra.
facts.quote: Martill indicated two distinguishing traits. The first of these is an autapomorphy, or a unique specialization: there are seven pairs of teeth present, all of them placed in front of the nasoantorbital fenestra.

facts.statement: Unlike other pterosaurs from the Santana Formation, Unwindia has homodont teeth that are all the same shape.
facts.quote: The second trait sets Unwindia apart from all other pterosaurs known from the Santana Formation: the teeth are homodont, having the same shape.

facts.statement: The teeth are long, straight, conical, and slightly transversely flattened, reaching up to 9 mm in length.
facts.quote: The teeth are long, straight, up to 9 mm long, conical, and slightly transversely flattened.

facts.statement: David Martill concluded that Unwindia was a basal ctenochasmatoid without performing a phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Martill concluded that Unwindia was a basal ctenochasmatoid, though without a phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: Mark Witton suggested in 2013 that Unwindia might belong to the family Lonchodectidae.
facts.quote: Witton in 2013 suggested that it could belong to the Lonchodectidae.

facts.statement: In 2020, Alexander Averianov suggested that Unwindia does not belong to the family Lonchodectidae.
facts.quote: In 2020 however, Russian paleontologist Alexander Averianov suggested that Unwindia did not belong to the Lonchodectidae.

facts.statement: Unwindia is classified within the superfamily Ctenochasmatoidea.
The family classification for Unwindia is uncertain and listed as possibly Lonchodectidae.
The holotype was recovered from the Santana Formation of the Araripe Basin, dated to the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir del holotipo SMNK PAL 6597, un cráneo parcial recuperado de rocas de la formación Santana de la Cuenca de Araripe, que data de la época del Cenomaniense.

facts.statement: The time range for Unwindia is estimated between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)
